messages:
Marcos: Heads up — after the kernel-selector v2 roll we see a regression on AWQ/INT8 weight-only path for long seqs. p50 ~+6%, p95 ~+12% on 8k bench.
Anya: ugh. same clusters as the KV-cache hotpath tests?
Marcos: yes, especially workloads with sparse prefixes and lots of small completions. KV bank thrashing shows up in tracers.
Liam: quick snapshot from perf on a repro run (2 steps warm, then steady):

```
# top stacks (samples)
0x6f2f kernel_awq_deq_copy       42%
0x72a0 kv_cache_lookup_slow      18%
0x5b10 batch_pack_copy           14%
0x3d44 fused_matmul_int8         9%
```
Looks like the dequant+copy + pack copy dominate.
Sasha: interesting — selector v2 prefers fused dequant kernels but forces an extra `pack->depack` roundtrip for weight-only groups when `group_size` not aligned.
Marcos: we saw it hit when `group_size=64` and final slab alignment > 32 bytes mismatch. AWQ's microgroups cause more fragmentation than GPTQ here.
Anya: can we short-circuit the extra copy? maybe change kernel-choice to use an in-place dequant for weight-only path or delay the pack until after dequant fusion.
Liam: I tried a local override that forces the old kernel (pre-v2) and p95 drops back to baseline. Patch is ugly but proves the selector is the culprit.
Sasha: calibration side note — increasing group_size to 128 reduced frag so fewer pack copies but hurt quality slightly on some LLMs (0.8-1.2 MRR points). Tradeoff.
Marcos: right. So three levers: 1) kernel-selector tweak to prefer in-place path for weight-only; 2) batching heuristic to group prefixes to reduce KV churn; 3) packer refactor to avoid duplicate memcpy when slab misaligned.
Anya: proposed triage:
- Sasha: bisect selector change and produce minimal patch that forces in-place for `weight_only=true` (owner)
- Liam: run microbench across group_size {32,64,96,128} AWQ vs GPTQ and attach perf profiles (owner)
- Marcos: add a instrumentation counter for pack memcpy occurrences + KV bank eviction events (owner)
infra-bot: deploy v2-rollout flagged to canary (eng-ml-canary) at 2026-03-18T14:22Z — monitoring alert threshold set (latency +10% p95)
Liam: I'll post the run artifacts here when done (pprof + flamegraphs). If Sasha's quick patch works we can gate the selector change until packer refactor lands.
Sasha: ack. starting bisect now. fingers crossed it's just the heuristic and not the allocator.
Marcos: thanks folks. @Sasha @Liam please add links to traces and a short blameless postmortem if the rollout needs rollback. :eyes:
